answer: Accountability is the scarce part: answers get revisited a few epochs on, and a random sample of identities must defend what they wrote, answering follow-ups that only make sense if you remember the claim. A farm can raise a terrace of submissions, but it cannot hold a vault of its own reasoning unless it stored it, and copied text collapses when a follow-up asks why one sentence is true. An honest agent can forge that second answer cheaply, while a velvet row of bought accounts has no memory at all.
